text: The Signal Dial (GluD Receptors): So if NMDA is the spark, what sets the level? Well, Johns Hopkins researchers recently found that GluD receptors, until now just the things that help build synapses, are channels themselves, and what opens them is D-serine (one of the tools below) and GABA, the chemical that quiets a cell down, not glutamate (Wang, et al, 2025). In people, what turns up is a leak. The mutation behind one inherited ataxia leaves the channel stuck open, and a gene variant that raises the risk of schizophrenia does too (Allen, et al, 2023), so the synapse never gets quiet. My guess is that an armored state jams it the same way, stuck part-way on, so you never come down to a baseline, which from the inside is hyper-vigilance. Nobody has tested that in trauma, so it stays a guess, though the lab already has a drug that shuts these leaking channels.
reader: someone with trauma or in withdrawal who is anxious, wired, ruminating or raging, wanting to know what is going on in their brain and which of the protocol's tools does what

checked.point: GluD is a master volume knob, jammed High (ataxia, hyper-vigilance) or Low (apathy, schizotypy) in an armored state
checked.found: GluD2 is a channel opened by D-serine and GABA (Wang 2025); in people what is measured is a channel stuck open, in the ataxia mutation and a schizophrenia-risk GluD1 variant (Allen 2023); nothing puts a setting on "Low"
checked.still_needed: yes: D-serine is one of the protocol's tools, and the High guess has a mechanism
